title: Characterization of the inverse CDF
statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\mathrm{Fin}\,m = \{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$ with $m \ge 1$, and write $F(n) = \sum_{j < n} p(j) \in \bbr_{\ge 0}^{\infty}$ for its cumulative distribution function. Let $x \in \bbr_{\ge 0}^{\infty}$ satisfy $x < 1$, and let $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,m$. Then the largest index whose cumulative probability does not exceed $x$ equals $i$ if and only if
\[
F(i) \le x < F(i+1).
\]
hypotheses_covered: p is a probability mass function on Fin m
x lies in the extended nonnegative reals
i is an index in Fin m
replaced:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\mathrm{Fin}\,m$ with $m \ge 1$, let $x \in
\bbr_{\ge 0}^{\infty}$ satisfy $x < 1$, and let $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,m$. Then
$\mathrm{invCdf}(p, x) = i$ if and only if
\[
\mathrm{cdf}(p, i) \le x < \mathrm{cdf}(p, i+1).
\]
